name: Andriy Shevchenko
years: Ballon d'Or 2004; born 29 Sep 1976; research as of 2026-11-20 (90-day window 2026-08-22 to 2026-11-20)

recent_news.headline: Shevchenko calls Mudryk's accusations against the UAF 'baseless slander' and demands evidence or an apology
facts: In an interview with Dmytro Hordon, Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk (now at Tottenham on loan) said the banned substance meldonium could only have entered his body at a Ukraine national-team camp, and said the UAF was involved.

Shevchenko, as UAF president, said the claims unfairly target staff who work honestly and professionally, and that Mudryk's representatives had repeatedly asked the UAF to find an employee to take the blame, which the UAF refused.
Shevchenko said Chelsea had asked the UAF to give Mudryk no medication at camps and staff complied; he asked Mudryk to provide his evidence.

recent_news.headline: Shevchenko: Ukraine failed its Nations League goal and is 'in exactly the division it deserves'
facts: Ukraine finished third in its League B group, kept its League B place, missed the promotion play-offs and missed the second seeding pot for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw (per Liga.net).
Shevchenko said Maldera and staff gained experience in difficult squad circumstances and gave new players their national-team debuts; the UAF is not considering the coach's resignation.
Shevchenko thanked fans for support and said qualifying for Euro 2028 is the main task.

recent_news.headline: Ukraine beat Georgia 1-0 in the last Nations League game and stay in League B
facts: Danylo Sikan scored in the 1st minute in Kosice, Slovakia (Wikipedia; UNN calls it the fastest goal in the team's official matches); Ukraine finished third with 7 points.
Final group table: Northern Ireland 12, Hungary 11, Ukraine 7, Georgia 2 (Wikipedia, confirmed).
The win avoided relegation to League C; Georgia finished fourth and enters the relegation play-offs.

recent_news.headline: Maldera says he has not discussed resigning with Shevchenko after the run of Nations League defeats
facts: Coach Andrea Maldera said he and Shevchenko had not discussed his resignation (UNN, 16 Nov).
Ukraine had lost three games in a row under him before the Georgia game (2 Oct, 5 Oct, 14 Nov).
Shevchenko had previously expressed support for Maldera and trust in him (Liga.net).

recent_news.headline: Northern Ireland 1-0 Ukraine in Belfast: third straight defeat under Maldera
facts: Devlin scored in the 68th minute at Windsor Park; it was 0-0 at half-time.
Ukraine had more of the ball but did not score; after five games Ukraine had 4 points and goal difference -4.
A loss to Georgia three days later would have meant relegation to League C.

recent_news.headline: Ukraine lose 1-2 to Hungary in Trnava after conceding straight after an 83rd-minute equaliser
facts: Hungary led through Milan Toth (52'), Roman Yaremchuk equalised from a corner in the 83rd minute, and Hungary scored the winner two minutes later (Wikipedia and 11v11 per earlier research: Mark Csinger 85'; UNN names Gabor Jurek, so the scorer is disputed).
It was Ukraine's second straight defeat; they fell to third in the group.
The game was a nominal home game played in Trnava, Slovakia because of the Russian invasion.

recent_news.headline: Ukraine 0-3 Northern Ireland in Trnava, third goal rolls through Riznyk's legs
facts: Ukraine had 73% possession and 11 shots but only 2 on target.
The third goal went between goalkeeper Dmytro Riznyk's legs; Isaac Price headed the second.
It was Ukraine's first defeat of the campaign after a 1-0 win in Hungary and a 0-0 draw in Georgia.

recent_news.headline: Hungary 0-1 Ukraine: Maldera wins his first competitive game with three debutants
facts: Ukraine won 1-0 in Budapest in the first Nations League game under Maldera (25 Sep 2026).
Maldera said the team can play better and congratulated three debutants: Krupskyi, Drambayev and Krasnopir.
The UNN article does not name the scorer (the earlier 'Sikan per Liga.net caption' could not be confirmed and was removed).

recent_news.headline: Shevchenko turns 50; Zelensky calls him a legend
facts: Zelensky wrote 'Happy anniversary, legend. Victories to you, to our national team, and to our country; peace to us all. Glory to Ukraine.'

UNN traces his path from Dynamo Kyiv to Milan to UAF president (elected 25 Jan 2024 at the 26th Congress, replacing Andriy Pavelko; Oleh Protasov was acting president from May 2023; UNN says 'unanimously', Wikipedia lists 94 votes for and 1 abstention).
Former Milan teammate Alessandro Costacurta congratulated him; UNN also notes the VHS-tape story of his Milan move.

recent_news.headline: Retro story: Milan signed Shevchenko after ordering a VHS tape of his Barcelona hat-trick
facts: Milan scouts were not at the 4-0 win at Camp Nou on 5 Nov 1997; sporting director Ariedo Braida ordered a VHS recording from the Mediaset newsroom.
Milan paid about 45 billion lire (about $24m) in summer 1999.
In his first Milan season he scored 24 goals in 32 Serie A games.

recent_news.headline: Shevchenko's son Kristian signs for seventh-tier Sholing
facts: Kristian, 19, joined Southern League side Sholing (seventh tier) after being released by Watford in the summer; he never made a senior appearance for Watford and has 15 Ukraine youth caps (BritBrief, published 3 Oct 2026).
A Sholing statement says he came through the youth setups at Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur and Watford.
Sholing were 16th with 10 points from their first 8 league games (per Mirror via BritBrief).

recent_news.headline: Shevchenko presents the Young Talent award to Lamine Yamal at the London Ballon d'Or ceremony
facts: Ceremony at the London Palladium on 26 October 2026 (Wikipedia; ua.news says London); Shevchenko is described as UAF president and Ukrainian legend and presented the men's Young Talent (Kopa Trophy) award.
Yamal won the men's Kopa Trophy for the third time (96 points, Pau Cubarsi second with 94 per Wikipedia). The earlier '24 goals and 18 assists' figure could not be confirmed and was removed.
Shevchenko won his own Ballon d'Or in 2004.

recent_news.headline: Shevchenko presents the 'Legend of Football' order to Rinat Akhmetov
facts: UAF article dated 14 Oct 2026, 21:37: Shevchenko awarded Rinat Akhmetov the 'Legend of Football' order, recognising his 30 years leading FC Shakhtar.
The earlier '18 Nov' date came from an unverified search listing and is dropped; the UAF page itself shows 14 Oct.

recent_news.headline: Mudryk joins Tottenham on season-long loan after his doping ban ends (background to the Nov 19 row)
facts: Mudryk joined Tottenham from Chelsea on a season-long loan on 1 Sep 2026 (Wikipedia; Malay Mail dated 2 Sep).

His doping case ended in late July 2026: Wikipedia says all charges were dropped on 31 July 2026; Shevchenko refers to settlements with WADA and the English FA. Exact terms of the settlement differ between sources and were not independently confirmed.
He had not played since late 2024 before his return.

recent_news.headline: Children of rescuers lead Ukraine onto the pitch against Georgia (UAF)
facts: UAF announced children of State Emergency Service rescuers would lead the team out for the Georgia game.
Posted on the UAF news feed on 17 Nov 2026.

recent_news.headline: UAF opens a UEFA Playmakers centre in Vinnytsia Oblast
facts: Listed at the top of the UAF news feed on 20 Nov 2026.
Part of UAF grassroots programmes under Shevchenko's presidency (headline only; details not read).

now.role: President of the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF). Elected on 25 January 2024 at the 26th Congress (UNN: unanimously; Wikipedia: 94 votes for, 1 abstention), replacing Andriy Pavelko; Oleh Protasov was acting president from May 2023 to Jan 2024. No report of a leadership change found.
now.national_team: Italian Andrea Maldera (55) was appointed head coach on 18 May 2026 after Serhiy Rebrov left in April when Ukraine failed to reach the 2026 World Cup. Maldera is the first foreign coach of the national team and had earlier worked with the national team and clubs (UNN). Shevchenko chose him from four candidates, called him 'an Italian with a Ukrainian soul' and set Euro 2028 qualification as the task.
now.season_numbers: 2026/27 Nations League, League B Group 2: W 1-0 Hungary (a, 25 Sep), D 0-0 Georgia (a, 28 Sep), L 0-3 Northern Ireland (2 Oct), L 1-2 Hungary (5 Oct), L 0-1 Northern Ireland (14 Nov), W 1-0 Georgia (17 Nov). Record 2W 1D 3L, goals 3-6 (GD -3), 7 points, third place, stayed in League B. Final table: Northern Ireland 12 (promoted to League A), Hungary 11 (promotion play-offs), Ukraine 7, Georgia 2 (relegation play-offs). Ukraine missed the play-offs and the second pot for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw.
now.contract: GAP: no source found for the length or end date of his UAF presidency term. HYPOTHESIS: Wikipedia notes the UAF term was extended from four to five years in 2017; his term end was not confirmed.
now.what_people_say: Shevchenko himself says the team is 'in exactly the division it deserves' and the goal was missed. Mudryk accuses the UAF over his meldonium case and Shevchenko calls it baseless slander. Zelensky called him a legend on his 50th birthday (29 Sep 2026).
now.other: Turned 50 on 29 Sep 2026. Presented the Young Talent (Kopa Trophy) award to Lamine Yamal at the 26 Oct Ballon d'Or ceremony in London (ua.news; Wikipedia confirms date and venue). Presented the 'Legend of Football' order to Rinat Akhmetov on 14 Oct (UAF). No coaching or club job outside UAF found. No business, media-job or personal social-media stories found in the window (GAP: web search budget ran out).

quick_context: Shevchenko won the 2004 Ballon d'Or after scoring 24 goals in 32 Serie A games as Milan took the 2003-04 title.
He scored the winning penalty in the 2003 Champions League final shootout against Juventus.
He is Ukraine's record scorer with 48 goals in 111 games.
roast_past: Chelsea paid 30.8 million pounds in 2006; he scored 22 goals in 77 games in all competitions, only 9 in 48 Premier League appearances. Friendly line: the most expensive 22 goals in London.

2005 Istanbul final: Dudek saved his extra-time double chance and then his shootout penalty. Shevchenko himself has called the double save inexplicable and said his penalty was too close to the middle of the goal.
2012: he left football for politics; his party 'Ukraine - Forward!' took 1.58% of the vote and won no seats.
Genoa 2021-22: 11 matches, 1 win, 3 draws, 7 losses, sacked on 15 January 2022 after a 0-2 debut at home to Roma.
2008-09 loan back to Milan: 26 appearances, 2 goals and no league goals.
Euro 2020: Ukraine's first quarter-final ended 0-4 against England in Rome (Kane 2, Maguire, Henderson). Balance with praise: it was still Ukraine's best Euro run.
His transfer to Milan needed a VHS tape: scouts did not travel, Milan ordered a recording of the Barcelona hat-trick.
roast_now: As UAF president he says the national team is 'in exactly the division it deserves' - League B, third in a four-team group.
He picked Maldera from four candidates; the new coach then lost three games in a row and had to say publicly that he had not discussed resigning.
Ukraine had 73% possession and only 2 of 11 shots on target against Northern Ireland, then lost 0-3 with a goal through the goalkeeper's legs. Aim the joke at the situation, not at a named player.
Ukraine missed the Euro 2028 second seeding pot, even though the main target is Euro 2028.
He handed the Young Talent award to Yamal, who already has three Kopa trophies; Sheva has one Ballon d'Or and a presidency of League B.
From striker to politician to coach to boss: a CV with more titles than the national team has points this autumn (7).
praise: 2003-04: 24 goals in 32 Serie A games, top scorer, Milan champions, then the 2004 Ballon d'Or (third Ukrainian winner after Blokhin and Belanov).
Scored the decisive penalty in the 2003 Champions League final against Juventus.
Ukraine's all-time top scorer: 48 goals in 111 games; Yarmolenko is next with 47.
Hat-trick in the 4-0 win at Barcelona's Camp Nou on 5 Nov 1997; Dynamo won 7-0 on aggregate.
As coach took Ukraine to the Euro 2020 quarter-finals, their first ever at a Euro; 52 games, 25 wins, 13 draws, 14 losses. Beat Sweden 2-1 after extra time (Dovbyk 120+1).
Zelensky called him 'legend' on his 50th birthday; about 174 Milan goals, second on the club's all-time list (sources vary 173-175).
no_joke_topics: Doping and the meldonium case (Mudryk): report as news only, no jokes at anyone's expense
Health, injuries and any medical matter
War, the Russian invasion, attacks such as Poltava, rescuers and children of rescuers, FIFA/Russia return debate
Family: sons, including Kristian at Sholing, and marriage
Legal troubles and accusations of wrongdoing (the UAF scapegoat claim is an allegation from one side)
Players' personal failures: joke about results and the situation, not named players
